name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.13.0: cross-checks PostgreSQL17 closures, SQL/SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against gold SQL. Adds standalone shacl-repair with authored synthetic before/after report bags, retained targets, hard immutable facts and separate edit costs; standalone grain with independent operation/key/filter/null-policy contracts plus bounded read-only PostgreSQL key, orphan and fanout evidence for undated preaggregate-to-node measures; and opt-in reason --explain-inconsistency using the same HermiT to localize generated axiom groups only after consistency fails. Original failures remain, and subset-minimality requires completed final deletion checks on a correctly bound original graph. Limits/errors never establish minimality. Same-engine explanation is not independent certification or a global minimum. New standalone diagnostics are outside the default report pipeline. No automatic repair, full SHACL report equivalence, Cube aggregate-value oracle, general grain/business correctness, shared whole-run snapshot or runtime attestation is claimed. Dependency pins and defaults stay unchanged. Rerun build, reason, cube, verify and report after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
